- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi.routing import format_sse_event

result = format_sse_event(data_str="Hello\n")
print(repr(result))
# Actual:   b'data: Hello\n\n'
# Expected: b'data: Hello\ndata: \n\n'
```


### Description

## What's happening

`format_sse_event` uses `str.splitlines()` to split `data_str` into SSE `data:` lines. `splitlines()` does not preserve trailing empty strings, so trailing newlines are silently dropped — corrupting the streamed content.

**Environment:**
- FastAPI version: 0.136.1 (also confirmed on 0.135.3)
- Python version: 3.12


## Root Cause

In `fastapi/routing.py`:

```python
if data_str is not None:
    for line in data_str.splitlines():  # ← drops trailing empty strings
        lines.append(f"data: {line}")
```

`splitlines()` does not preserve trailing empty strings:

| Input | `split("\n")` | `splitlines()` |
|---|---|---|
| `"Hello\n"` | `["Hello", ""]` | `["Hello"]` |
| `"\n"` | `["", ""]` | `[""]` |
| `"Hello\n\n"` | `["Hello", "", ""]` | `["Hello", ""]` |
| `"Hello\nWorld"` | `["Hello", "World"]` | `["Hello", "World"]` |

The same issue exists in the `comment` field, which also uses `splitlines()`.

## Expected Behavior

Per the [SSE specification](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/server-sent-events.html), multiple `data:` lines are concatenated with `\n`. A trailing newline in the original string must be preserved as a trailing empty `data:` line:

```
data: Hello
data: 
```

This encodes `data = "Hello\n"`. The current implementation produces:

```
data: Hello
```

Which encodes `data = "Hello"` — the trailing newline is silently lost.

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.135.3

### Pydantic Version

(polaris) ➜  polaris git:(main) python -c "import pydantic; print(pydantic.version.VERSION)" 2.12.5

### Python Version

3.12.10

### Additional Context

_No response_

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
# this example is copied from the Pydantic docs with updates to work with FastAPI
# docs: https://pydantic.dev/docs/validation/latest/concepts/serialization/#polymorphic-serialization

from fastapi import FastAPI, Response
from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict

class User(BaseModel):
    name: str


class UserLogin(User):
    password: str


class OuterModel(BaseModel):
    # would love if FastAPI could read this!
    model_config = ConfigDict(polymorphic_serialization=True)

    user: User


app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/")
def current():
    model = OuterModel(
        user=UserLogin(name='pydantic', password='password'),
    )
    return model


@app.get("/expected")
def expected():
    model = OuterModel(
        user=UserLogin(name='pydantic', password='password'),
    )
    content = model.model_dump_json(polymorphic_serialization=True)
    return Response(media_type="application/json", content=content)
```


### Description

* Pydantic 2.13+ uses `polymorphic_serialization=True` to serialize a model with its actual type vs declared type
    * PR: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/pull/12518
    * Release notes: https://pydantic.dev/articles/pydantic-v2-13-release
* When serializing a response it'd be great to either:
    * Be able to declare in the route to pass this flag when serializing (e.g., `@app.get(..., polymorphic_serialization=True)`), or...
    * For FastAPI to peek into the model's config to see if the flag is there, and if so apply it (this would be awesome!)

Linux, macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.135.3

### Pydantic Version

2.13.4

### Python Version

3.11.14

### Additional Context

_No response_

I think all these flags that modify endpoint output making it different from what is declared in OpenAPI schema is bad idea and we shouldn't add more such flags.
There is already way to achieve this - by returning Response explicitly (as it's shown in the discussion)

### Example Code

```python
from collections.abc import Generator
from typing import Annotated, Any

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import EventSourceResponse
from pydantic import BaseModel


class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str


def dep_session() -> Any:
    # yield dependency - cleanup should run after stream ends
    yield [Item(name="foo"), Item(name="bar")]


app = FastAPI()


@app.get("/sse", response_class=EventSourceResponse)
def sse_items(items: Annotated[list, Depends(dep_session)]) -> Any:
    def gen() -> Generator[Item, None, None]:
        yield from items

    return gen()
```


### Description

`test_dependency_after_yield_streaming.py` verifies that yield dependency cleanup runs correctly with `StreamingResponse`. There is no equivalent test for `EventSourceResponse` (SSE), which uses a different internal code path (`_sse_producer_cm` task group in `routing.py`).

I have written `tests/test_dependency_after_yield_sse.py` locally - 8 tests covering sync/async yield deps with SSE, cleanup verification, and broken dependency behaviour. All pass.

Would a PR adding this test file be welcome?

questions.title: feat: add class-based view and route support, consistent with official FastAPI style
questions.answer:
@Shahab Rashidian Dezfuly

Thank you for taking the time to review my proposal and sharing your valuable experience with class-based patterns in FastAPI production environments. Your insights about the relationship between dependency injection and class instantiation are indeed a crucial discussion point in the FastAPI community.
 
Regarding your concerns, I'd like to clarify a few points about CBX's design philosophy:
 
CBX is a lightweight, non-invasive wrapper.
CBX doesn't reimplement or bypass FastAPI's routing and DI system. It simply provides a minimal mechanism for binding class methods to routes. All actual routing, parameter parsing, dependency resolution, async handling, etc., remain delegated to FastAPI's native machinery. Therefore, once properly bound, features like OpenAPI generation, hot reload, and async support should behave identically to standard function-based routes.
 
Design focus: Class-based routing for simple scenarios
CBX targets straightforward use cases where developers prefer class-based organization without complex dependency injection needs. We intentionally leave initialization control entirely to the user—they decide when and how to instantiate (e.g., at app startup, or via a factory per request). This maintains flexibility while avoiding overlap with FastAPI's built-in Depends() system.
As you correctly noted, mixing Depends() in init would conflict with FastAPI's request-scoped DI. CBX's approach is to stay out of that territory, serving as a lightweight complement to the official DI patterns, focused purely on expressive routing.
 
Testing and compatibility
Your points about test coverage and compatibility are well-taken. I've already added comprehensive tests locally (async methods, OpenAPI schema, path/query params, etc.) and will continue improving them. If the FastAPI team considers it valuable, I'm happy to integrate these tests into the official CI pipeline to ensure ongoing compatibility.
 
CBX isn't meant to replace existing DI patterns. Rather, it offers an alternative for developers who prefer class-based views in simple scenarios—rapid prototyping, internal tools, or migrating existing class structures to FastAPI. Its value lies in minimal API surface and near-zero learning curve.
 
Thanks again for your thoughtful feedback—it genuinely helps improve the proposal. I welcome any further suggestions or edge cases you might identify.
 
Best regards

questions.question:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
import warnings
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.encoders import jsonable_encoder
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

# --- Issue 1: jsonable_encoder crashes on circular references ---
# Reported in #2972, #1891, Discussion #10358, Discussion #5973

class Node:
    pass

a = Node()
b = Node()
a.child = b
b.parent = a

try:
    jsonable_encoder(a)
    print("BUG: no error raised")
except RecursionError as e:
    print(f"CONFIRMED: RecursionError — {type(e).__name__}")
    print(f"  (no useful message, just stack exhaustion)")

# --- Issue 2: response_model_exclude accepted but has no effect ---
# Related to Discussion #13859

with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter("always")

    app = FastAPI()

    class User(BaseModel):
        name: str
        password: str

    @app.get("/user", response_model_exclude={"password"})
    async def get_user():
        return User(name="alice", password="secret123")

    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/user")
    body = response.json()
    print(f"Response body: {body}")
    print(f"Password leaked: {'password' in body}")
    print(f"Warnings emitted: {len(w)}")
    if not w:
        print("  CONFIRMED: zero warnings — exclude silently accepted")
```


### Description

Two cases where FastAPI could catch problems early, consistent with how it already validates request parameters and response models.

**1. `jsonable_encoder` crashes on circular references**

Objects with bidirectional relationships (common in SQLAlchemy with `backref`, MongoEngine) cause `RecursionError` or fatal stack overflow with no clear message. This has been reported multiple times since 2021:
- #2972 (SQLAlchemy mapper recursion)
- #1891 (fatal stack overflow)
- Discussion #10358 (asks for "Circular reference detected" like json.dumps)
- Discussion #5973 (stack overflow on cyclical references)

`jsonable_encoder` could track visited objects and raise a clear `ValueError` on cycle detection, plus a depth bound for extremely deep structures.

**2. `response_model_exclude` / `response_model_include` accepted without effect**

When set on a route without an explicit `response_model`, these filters are accepted but never applied. A developer sets `response_model_exclude={"password"}` believing the field is filtered — it isn't. Related to Discussion #13859 where `response_model_exclude_none=True` is similarly accepted without effect.

A `UserWarning` at route registration when these are set but no `response_model` is active would catch the misconfiguration early.

**Context**

I found these by scoring each assumption FastAPI's code makes against how strongly it's enforced — unguarded, convention, runtime check, or type-level guarantee. Writing out the serialization dispatch and route configuration as explicit decision trees made these gaps visible. The invariant analysis methodology — how each assumption is scored and what "enforced" means at each level — is documented at github.com/savarin/lean-agent.

I have working implementations for both and would be happy to open PRs if these are things the team wants to address. They're independent changes (different files, different subsystems), so they'd be separate, focused PRs.

### Operating System

Linux, macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.135.3

### Pydantic Version

2.12.5

### Python Version

3.11.11

### Additional Context

Both reproductions verified against upstream master (v0.135.3). The circular
reference issue produces a RecursionError or fatal stack overflow depending on
object depth. The response_model_exclude issue produces zero warnings — the
exclude parameter is silently accepted.

Optional Query Parameters with a Pydantic Model

from typing import Annotated, Any

import pytest
from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from starlette import status
from starlette.testclient import TestClient


class FilterParams(BaseModel):
    a: int | None = Field(default=None)


app = FastAPI()


@app.get(path="/items", response_model=FilterParams)
def get_example(filter_query: Annotated[FilterParams, Query()]):

@pytest.fixture

):

You can remove the starlette and pytest imports to strip the example even more, but I assume it might be helpful.

My expectation is that FastAPI converts the optional query parameter correctly to a pydantic model with the property `model_fields_set` populated based on whether the parameter is missing or not.

questions.answer:
Regarding your first point:

The current behavior is validated by Pydantic, and there is no equivalence between `None` and an empty string. This convention may be useful for your specific use case, but it could be completely inappropriate in other contexts.

Regarding the second point:

If the current example is not detailed enough to represent your issue, please provide a more complete one.
In any case, you can keep the current logic:

```python
@app.get(path="/items", response_model=FilterParams, response_model_exclude_unset=True)
def get_example(filter_query: Annotated[FilterParams, Query()]) -> dict:
    return filter_query.model_dump(exclude_unset=True)
```

Alternatively, you can omit both the parameters and the response model entirely from the route decorator.

### Commit to Help

### Example Code

```python
class Orchestrator:
    def __init__(
        self,
        controller_1: Annotated[Controller1, Depends(Controller1)],
        controller_2: Annotated[Controller2, Depends(Controller2)],
        controller_3: Annotated[Controller3, Depends(Controller3)],
        controller_4: Annotated[Controller4, Depends(Controller4)],
        controller_5: Annotated[Controller5, Depends(Controller5)],
    ):
        self._controller_1 = controller_1
        self._controller_2 = controller_2
        self._controller_3 = controller_3
        self._controller_4 = controller_4
        self._controller_5 = controller_5

    
    async def process_payload(self, payload) -> None:
        common_pre_logic(payload)
        
        match payload.type:
            case "type_1":
                await self._controller_1.handle(payload)
            case "type_2":
                await self._controller_2.handle(payload)
            case "type_3":
                await self._controller_3.handle(payload)
            case "type_4":
                await self._controller_4.handle(payload)
            case "type_5":
                await self._controller_5.handle(payload)
        
            case _:
                raise ValueError(f"Unknown payload type: {payload.type}")

        common_post_logic(payload)
```


### Description

I'd like the ability for the dependency injection system to lazily initialize deps, similar to how Dagger does it with a `@lazy` annotation or similar.

ie. Declare many dependencies in a class/endpoint, and only initialize the ones that are used.

The example use-case is a top-level Orchestrator which initializes the right Controller depending on the payload. All requests for one part of the app are processed via the Orchestrator, which is injected into the API endpoint.

We are currently forced to choose between two options:
1. Automatically instantiate many controllers which aren't used (could be 20+)
2. Create a dedicated method to initialize the right controller for the given payload. But the controller has to be manually created using the constructor or a factory method like `controller = Controller1()`, which prevents us from their dependencies using DI.

Lazy initialization solves this.

(Also, in my example, I do not want the `Controller` classes to depend on the `Orchestrator` - that inverts the hierarchy of responsibility. Especially if the orchestrator might need to use 2 controllers, etc.)

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi.dependencies.models import Dependant

dependant = Dependant()
try:
    scopes = dependant.security_requirements
    print("Success:", scopes)
except AttributeError as e:
    print(f"ERROR: {e}")
```


### Description

Before PR #14459:
The public attribute `dependant.security_requirements` existed and worked normally.

After PR #14459:
 Accessing `dependant.security_requirements` raises AttributeError.
 Error message: 'Dependant' object has no attribute 'security_requirements'

Root cause:
The public field `security_requirements` was directly removed from the Dependant class in dataclass definition, without any backward compatibility, deprecation warning, or fallback property.

This is a regression bug and API breaking change.

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

master branch (latest)      0.115.0+ (after PR #14459)

### Pydantic Version

N/A

### Python Version

3.8+

### Additional Context

The PR fixed OAuth2 scope handling in OpenAPI but accidentally broke backward compatibility by completely removing the public `security_requirements` attribute from the Dependant dataclass.

The correct fix should be:
 Add a @property fallback for backward compatibility
 Add a DeprecationWarning
 Keep external code from breaking

Currently, any external tool, plugin, or test that accesses dependant.security_requirements will crash with AttributeError.
questions.answer:
`Dependant` is not a part of public API. It's not documented in docs.

For now FastAPI doesn't have public API for integrations with other libs.
We have this in our plan, but for now you should pin FastAPI version and test before upgrading to newer version to prevent breaking your integration

questions.title: FastAPI + Starlette 1.0.0: Jinja2 TemplateResponse raises 'unhashable type: dict'
questions.question:
## Description

After upgrading to Starlette 1.0.0, FastAPI applications using Jinja2 templates fail with:

```
TypeError: cannot use 'tuple' as a dict key (unhashable type: 'dict')
```

at `jinja2/utils.py`, line 515.

## Environment

- FastAPI 0.135.1
- Starlette 1.0.0
- Jinja2 3.1.6
- Tested on Python 3.12 and 3.14 (issue reproduced on both)

## Steps to reproduce

1. Install `fastapi==0.135.1` with `starlette==1.0.0`
2. Create a route that returns a `Jinja2Templates.TemplateResponse`
3. Any template render raises the error above

## Workaround

Pin `starlette<1.0.0` in `requirements.txt`.

## Notes

This appears to be related to breaking changes in Starlette 1.0.0's `TemplateResponse` signature. FastAPI may need to update how it passes context to Jinja2 templates for Starlette 1.0.0 compatibility.

Detected in production during a routine deployment where pip resolved Starlette 1.0.0 instead of 0.52.x.
questions.answer: The OP is probably using the old API that was deprecated some years ago, and it was removed in 1.0.

questions.question:
### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from starlette.routing import get_route_path root_app = FastAPI() sub_app = FastAPI() root_app.mount("/subapp", sub_app) @root_app.get("/test") async def root_test(path: str, request: Request): return { "app": "root", "root_path": request.scope.get("root_path", ""), "path": request.scope.get("path", ""), "route_path": get_route_path(request.scope), } @sub_app.get("/test") async def sub_test(path: str, request: Request): return { "app": "sub", "root_path": request.scope.get("root_path", ""), "path": request.scope.get("path", ""), "route_path": get_route_path(request.scope), } ``` ### Description I am creating a FastAPI application that is served behind a proxy which strips part of the path, so I've been following the [Proxy with a stripped path prefix](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/behind-a-proxy/#proxy-with-a-stripped-path-prefix) docs. I am also using mounted sub-applications to handle API versioning (e.g. mounted at `/v1` and `/v2` for separate docs). Initially, I was using the `root_path` parameter in the FastAPI constructor to configure the stripped-path prefix, which works as expected for the root application, but I experienced unexpected behaviour adding the sub-applications. --- `tl;dr` According to the [FastAPI docs](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/behind-a-proxy/#setting-the-root-path-in-the-fastapi-app): > Passing the `root_path` to `FastAPI` would be the equivalent of passing the `--root-path` command line option to Uvicorn or Hypercorn. However, my experience has shown that these configuration methods result in different behaviour for the request scope `path` which seems to break route matching in mounted sub-applications when using the `root_path` parameter. --- **With no root path configuration:**
```GET /test - 200 OK ✅``` ```GET /subapp/test - 200 OK ✅```
```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "", "path": "/test", "route_path": "/test", } ``` ```json json { "app": "sub", "root_path": "/subapp", "path": "/subapp/test", "route_path": "/test", } ```
**OpenAPI schema:** `/openapi.json` and `/subapp/openapi.json` With no root path configuration, the behaviour is as expected. --- **Root path configured via FastAPI CLI with `--root-path="/api"`:**
```GET /test - 200 OK ✅``` ```GET /subapp/test - 200 OK ✅```
```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "/api", "path": "/api/test", "route_path": "/test", } ``` ```json json { "app": "sub", "root_path": "/api/subapp", "path": "/api/subapp/test", "route_path": "/test", } ```
```GET /api/test - 404 Not Found ❌``` ```GET /api/subapp/test - 404 Not Found ❌```
```json json { "detail": "Not Found" } ``` ```json json { "detail": "Not Found" } ```
**OpenAPI schema:** `/api/openapi.json` and `/api/subapp/openapi.json` When configuring the root path via the FastAPI CLI option, the routes can be accessed at `localhost:8000/test` and `localhost:8000/subapp/test` as expected, since the `/api` root path would be stripped by the proxy. It is not possible to access the routes by including the root path in the requests when using the CLI option (as shown by the 404s). The OpenAPI schema is served with the root path prefixed so the Swagger UI can access it from outside the proxy (as described in the [FastAPI docs](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/behind-a-proxy/#check-the-docs-ui)) --- **Root path configured via FastAPI constructor with `root_path="/api"`:**
```GET /test - 200 OK ✅``` ```GET /subapp/test - 404 Not Found ❌```
```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "/api", "path": "/test", "route_path": "/test", } ``` ```json json { "detail": "Not Found" } ```
```GET /api/test - 200 OK ✅``` ```GET /api/subapp/test - 200 OK ✅```
```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "/api", "path": "/api/test", "route_path": "/test", } ``` ```json json { "app": "root", "root_path": "/api/subapp", "path": "/api/subapp/test", "route_path": "/test", } ```
**OpenAPI schema:** `/api/openapi.json` and `/api/subapp/openapi.json` Note that `/docs` and `/api/docs` work (and both fetch the OpenAPI JSON schema correctly), but `/subapp/docs` doesn't work – only `/api/subapp/docs` works. When configuring the root path via the FastAPI `root_path` constructor parameter, the root FastAPI app route can be accessed at `localhost:8000/test` as expected, **BUT** the sub-application route can no longer be accessed without the root path in the URL. Additionally, the behaviour continues to deviate since now it is possible to access the root app route by including the root path in the request which was not possible with the CLI option. The OpenAPI schema is served with the root path prefixed so the Swagger UI can access it from outside the proxy, but now the UI does not show a "Failed to load API definition" Fetch error. ### Operating System macOS ### Operating System Details macOS Sequoia 15.1.1 (24B91) ### FastAPI Version 0.135.1 ### Pydantic Version 2.11.4 ### Python Version 3.12.9 ### Additional Context This behaviour is described in another [discussion post](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/11959) from 2024, but I wasn't sure if necroposting in the comments was appropriate. I thought I would make a new discussion and hopefully be able to resolve the old discussion along with this one.
questions.answer:
> Passing the `root_path` to FastAPI would be the equivalent of passing the `--root-path` command line option to Uvicorn or Hypercorn.

This statement in docs is not correct.
In fact, you should:
* use `--root-path` when you run app behind a proxy which **strips** part of the path
* use `root_path` parameter in the `FastAPI` constructor when you run app behind a proxy that **doesn't strip** part of the path

I opened PR to fix docs: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14238

### Commit to Help

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated
from fastapi import FastAPI, Form
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()

class UploadForm(BaseModel):
    name: str
    file: bytes

@app.post("/upload/")
async def upload(data: Annotated[UploadForm, Form()]):
    return {"name": data.name, "size": len(data.file)}

client = TestClient(app)
response = client.post(
    "/upload/",
    files={"file": ("test.txt", b"hello world", "text/plain")},
    data={"name": "test"},
)
print(response.status_code)
print(response.json())


---
```


### Description

```
I am using a Pydantic BaseModel with Form() to group form fields together. 
When one of the fields is annotated as `bytes`, FastAPI does not call 
`read()` on the uploaded file and returns a 422 error instead.

What I expect:
- Status 200, FastAPI automatically reads the UploadFile into bytes,
  exactly as it does when `bytes` is a standalone File() parameter.

What actually happens:
- Status 422, `bytes_type` validation error. The raw UploadFile object 
  is passed directly to Pydantic without being read first.

This works fine (standalone):

    @app.post("/works/")
    async def works(file: bytes = File()):
        return {"size": len(file)}  # ✅ 200

This breaks (inside a Pydantic model):

    class UploadForm(BaseModel):
        file: bytes

    @app.post("/breaks/")
    async def breaks(data: Annotated[UploadForm, Form()]):
        return {"size": len(data.file)}  # ❌ 422

Affected annotations inside a Pydantic Form model:

| Annotation          | Works? |
|---------------------|--------|
| file: UploadFile    |  Yes |
| file: UploadFile|None | Yes |
| file: list[UploadFile] |  Yes |
| file: bytes         |  No  |
| file: bytes | None  |  No  |
| file: list[bytes]   |  No  |

I looked into the source code. The issue is in `_extract_form_body()` 
in `fastapi/dependencies/utils.py`. The guard:

    isinstance(field_info, params.File)

is always False for fields extracted from a Pydantic model because 
those fields have plain Pydantic FieldInfo, not params.File.
So `read()` is never called on the UploadFile.

I would be happy to work on a fix if this is confirmed.
```

---

## Operating System:
```
Windows
```

## FastAPI Version:
```
0.135.1

### Operating System

Windows

### Operating System Details

Windows 11

### FastAPI Version

0.135.1

### Pydantic Version

2.12.5

### Python Version

Python 3.11.9

### Additional Context

```
The standalone `bytes = File()` parameter works correctly.
The bug only occurs when `bytes` is declared inside a Pydantic 
BaseModel used with Form().

I also checked that `UploadFile`, `Optional[UploadFile]`, and 
`list[UploadFile]` inside a Pydantic Form model all work fine — 
only the `bytes` annotation is affected.

I have looked at the source code and I believe I can fix this.
I would be happy to submit a PR if this is confirmed.
questions.answer:
Declaring file upload fields using Pydantic model is not officially supported ([see comment to closed PR](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14343#issuecomment-3600534954)).

To make your example work, you need to add `File()` annotation to `file` field:

```py
class UploadForm(BaseModel):
    name: str
    file: Annotated[bytes, File()]
```

And specify `media_type="application/x-www-form-urlencoded"` as follows to make schema correct:

```py
@app.post("/upload/")
async def upload(data: Annotated[UploadForm, Form(media_type="application/x-www-form-urlencoded")]):
    return {"name": data.name, "size": len(data.file)}
```

One more time: this is not officially supported. You can use it on your own risk)

questions.title: Usage of ContextVar's in FastAPI
questions.question: ### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/tree/main ``` ### Description Hello, We're in the process of migrating our entire codebase from Pyramid to FastAPI. Due to some legacy architectural choices we ended up with a lot of endpoints that accept and return slightly different content based on a users roles, sometimes in combination with the state of the db model. This is something we're going to address in the future, but for the time being, I came up with an idea that uses Pydantic discriminators to dynamically determine the request and response schemas. I have a little testapp [here](https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/tree/main). The relevant sections are: - [Route that defines the create endpoint](https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/blob/6edd3b189173786a72a276a4ca09804470ae805e/app/routers/premies.py#L26) - [Discriminated unions](https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/blob/6edd3b189173786a72a276a4ca09804470ae805e/app/schemas.py#L289) - [And finally the discriminator itself](https://github.com/claeyswo/fastapi_poc/blob/6edd3b189173786a72a276a4ca09804470ae805e/app/schemas.py#L17) Which also renders nicely in the docs. Now the thing is that I use ContextVar's to inject userinfo into my discriminator. And I found [this](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/?h=contextvar#features_41). `Note: You probably don't need contextvars, and you should probably avoid using them. ` I know there are libraries that make extensive use of them, like starlette-context, but I don't know if I can use that as a reference. And my other team members all have their doubts about using them. So my question is: Should this be avoided? Is it ok? Are there any pitfalls? ### Operating System Linux ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version 0.128.7 ### Pydantic Version 2.12.5 ### Python Version Python 3.11.11 ### Additional Context _No response_
questions.answer:
Context vars can be difficult to deal with, they can be complex and hard to debug, depending on how you use them. But given you already have some complex code, they are probably right for your use case.

Here are the caveats:

In FastAPI, you need to set them in an `async` dependency function or path operation, or an async middleware. If the function is non-async, FastAPI will run it on a thread worker. And if the context var is set on a thread worker, that is, let's say, a "child" context, so the value will **not** be propagated upwards.

So, you need to set the context in an async function.

Now, if the code that gets the data to be set is non-async blocking code (e.g. calling a DB), and if you run it directly on the async function, it will block the event loop, blocking any other operation.

So, you will likely need to set the context var in an async function to some container (e.g. a dict) and then in the non-async blocking function that gets the data and sets the actual value (e.g. a user object), you can get the container value from the context var, and set the user inside of that container. This way, the blocking function is never really setting the value in the context var, it's only accessing it (the container), and modifying that container.

So, you will probably need something like this:

```Python
from contextvars import ContextVar
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import Depends, FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

# The context var holds a container (dict), not the final value directly
request_context: ContextVar[dict] = ContextVar("request_context")


async def set_context():
    """Async dependency that initializes the context var with a container.

    Must be async so the context var is set in the main async task,
    not in a thread worker.
    """
    ctx: dict = {}
    token = request_context.set(ctx)
    yield ctx
    request_context.reset(token)


def get_user_from_db(ctx: Annotated[dict, Depends(set_context)]) -> dict:
    """Sync dependency, runs in a thread worker.

    It receives the container from set_context and mutates it.
    It never calls request_context.set(), only reads and mutates the
    existing container, so the child-context limitation doesn't apply.
    """
    # Simulate blocking DB lookup
    user = {"id": 1, "name": "Alice", "role": "admin"}
    ctx["user"] = user
    return user


@app.get("/")
async def root(user: Annotated[dict, Depends(get_user_from_db)]):
    return {
        "user": user,
        "role_from_ctx": request_context.get().get("user", {}).get("role"),
    }
```

### Description

I am trying to understand how to best write a class-based  middleware for authentication. The documentation basically only mentions the middleware included with Starlette. The middlewares packages there have a class with mostly two methods: '__init__' and '__call__', but there are also some mentionings of a method 'dispatch'. I couldn't find good documentation about when to use which, or what to do with this method. In the docs, and also on the Internet, I couldn't find any documentation about class-based middleware except for pointing somewhere to the source code, but nothing like when to use what, what is deprecated, etc.

Can someone please explain?

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.129.0

### Pydantic Version

2.12.5

### Python Version

3.13.5

### Additional Context

questions.answer:
Great question! Here's a clear breakdown of class-based middleware in FastAPI/Starlette:

## Class-Based Middleware — Two Approaches

### 1. Pure ASGI Middleware (using `__init__` and `__call__`)
This is the lower-level approach:

from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Receive, Scope, Send

class AuthMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp):
        self.app = app

    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send):
        if scope["type"] == "http":
            # your auth logic here
            token = dict(scope.get("headers", [])).get(b"authorization", b"").decode()
            if not token:
                # reject request
                pass
        await self.app(scope, receive, send)

### 2. BaseHTTPMiddleware (using `dispatch`)
This is the higher-level, easier approach:

from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware
from starlette.requests import Request

class AuthMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        token = request.headers.get("authorization")
        if not token:
            return Response("Unauthorized", status_code=401)
        response = await call_next(request)
        return response

## When to use which?
- Use `dispatch` (BaseHTTPMiddleware) → simpler, cleaner, recommended for most use cases
- Use `__call__` (Pure ASGI) → better performance, needed for WebSockets or streaming

## Register in FastAPI:
app.add_middleware(AuthMiddleware)

Hope this helps! 🚀

questions.title: Dependency keeps going after response returns when there exists any backgroud tasks.
questions.question:
### Issue Content

```python
import asyncio

from fastapi import Depends, BackgroundTasks, FastAPI
from fastapi.responses import PlainTextResponse


app = FastAPI()

async def dep():
    yield
    print("dep done")

async def task():
    await asyncio.sleep(5)
    print("task done")

@app.get("/test", response_class=PlainTextResponse, tags=["test"], dependencies=[Depends(dep)])
async def test(bk: BackgroundTasks):
    bk.add_task(task)
    return "OK"
```

When access test endpoint, Both fastapi 0.128.0 and 0.133.0 have this behavior:

1. Response returns
2. print "dep done"
3. print "task done".

But in fastapi 0.115.12:

1. print "dep done"
2. Response returns
3. print "task done".

When the dependency is a database transaction, transaction is not committed after response returns, data changes are not accessable before backgroud tasks completion.
questions.answer:
Please, follow the template and don't open issues.

---
The behavior of dependencies with yield was changed in FastAPI [0.121.0](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/release-notes/#01210).
See: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/dependencies/dependencies-with-yield/#early-exit-and-scope

In short - you can configure it to work as it used to work using `scope="function"`:
```py

```

questions.title: Consider Pydantic serialization for exception handlers before deprecating ORJSONResponse
questions.question:
Following the discussion in #14964, deprecating `ORJSONResponse` and `UJSONResponse` might be premature since exception handlers can't benefit from the new Pydantic serialization introduced in #14962.

Currently, exception handlers must return a `Response` object, which means they fall back to stdlib `json.dumps` via `JSONResponse`, the exact use case where `ORJSONResponse` was providing free performance gains.

Two possible paths forward:

1. Use Pydantic serialization in `JSONResponse`

`JSONResponse` could use `TypeAdapter.dump_json` internally instead of `json.dumps`. Though this might impose constraints on the accepted content types.

2. Support typed returns in exception handlers

Allow exception handlers to return dicts or Pydantic models directly, similar to regular route handlers:

```python
class MyErrorBody(BaseModel):
    message: str

@app.exception_handler(MyError, status_code=status.HTTP_422_UNPROCESSABLE_ENTITY)
async def _(request: Request, exception: MyError) -> MyErrorBody:
    return MyErrorBody(message=str(exception))
```

This would enable Pydantic serialization for exception responses and feed the OpenAPI schema generation with error response types, which is currently not possible.
questions.answer:
For now, if you worry about the performance for errors / exception handlers, you could create a custom response with your serialization, it's 4 lines of code: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/advanced/custom-response/#custom-response-class

And you could also use something other than orjson, or a different format, etc.

### Example Code

```python
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager

from fastapi import FastAPI

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # app is not yet able to serve http requests
    yield

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
```


### Description

Hello,

First of all, thank you for maintaining this amazing project : )

I tried to find information on how to register a callback on post-startup event (moment when FastAPI is ready to handle HTTP requests), but in most threads, documentation and AI suggestions it all comes to usage of _lifespan feature.

However _lifespan happens before application is ready to serve and even running there some async code without awaiting (or something similar) does not guarantee that execution will happen after HTTP serving is started.

I was thinking about usage of some scheduling library, but I can predict that starting/stopping process of scheduled jobs will be possible only during _lifespan events, what leads to the same situation.

Is there any way to register a callback, something like a background task which happens once application is serving, in a easy (or at least a proper for FastAPI) way?

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

Docker / Python-3.11-bookworm

### FastAPI Version

0.111.1

### Pydantic Version

2.10.6

### Python Version

3.11

### Additional Context

_No response_
questions.answer:
Hey! Ran into this exact same limitation a while ago. The tricky part is that ASGI itself doesn't actually have a native "server is actively listening" event, which is why lifespan blocks until you yield.

If you just need to kick off a background process right around startup without blocking the server from handling requests, the easiest way is to just drop an asyncio.create_task right before the yield. Since you don't await it, FastAPI will continue starting up:

```Python
import asyncio
from contextlib import asynccontextmanager
from fastapi import FastAPI

async def my_background_job():
    # Optional: give the server a second to bind to the port
    await asyncio.sleep(1) 
    print("Running post-startup!")

@asynccontextmanager
async def lifespan(app: FastAPI):
    # Fire and forget the task
    task = asyncio.create_task(my_background_job())
    yield
    # Clean up gracefully on shutdown
    task.cancel()

app = FastAPI(lifespan=lifespan)
```

If you strictly need to guarantee the socket is bound and the server is accepting HTTP traffic before your callback runs, you have to step outside FastAPI and handle it at the server level (e.g., Uvicorn). You can run Uvicorn programmatically and poll server.started:

```Python

import asyncio
import uvicorn
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()

async def main():
    config = uvicorn.Config("main:app", port=8000)
    server = uvicorn.Server(config)
    
    # Start server without blocking the main thread
    server_task = asyncio.create_task(server.serve())
    
    # Wait until Uvicorn explicitly flags that it's ready
    while not server.started:
        await asyncio.sleep(0.1)
        
    print("Server is 100% ready and accepting requests now!")
    # ---> Do your post-startup stuff here <---
    
    await server_task

if __name__ == "__main__":
    asyncio.run(main())
```

Hope this helps!

questions.question:

- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
import logging
from logging.handlers import RotatingFileHandler
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request

logger = logging.getLogger("app")
logger.setLevel(logging.INFO)

handler = RotatingFileHandler(
    "app.log",
    maxBytes=5 * 1024 * 1024,
    backupCount=3,
    encoding="utf-8",
)

formatter = logging.Formatter(
    "%(asctime)s | %(levelname)s | %(name)s | %(message)s"
)
handler.setFormatter(formatter)
logger.addHandler(handler)

app = FastAPI()

@app.middleware("http")
async def log_requests(request: Request, call_next):
    logger.info(f"{request.method} {request.url.path}")
    response = await call_next(request)
    logger.info(f"status={response.status_code}")
    return response

@app.get("/ping")
async def ping():
    logger.info("Ping")
    return {"status": "ok"}
```


### Description

I’m looking for best practices for using a middleware logger together with internal (application-level) loggers in FastAPI, but I can’t find clear information about possible issues when logging to file(s) while running the app **with multiple workers**.

Are there any problems with file logging when using multiple Uvicorn workers?
Should I rely on Uvicorn’s built-in loggers (uvicorn.error, uvicorn.access),
and do they handle file write races automatically, or do I need to take care of this myself?

Do I need to add a unique identifier (PID) to the log file name to avoid race conditions, or should I avoid file logging when using workers?

The same question applies to running multiple Docker containers/instances: should I explicitly add a prefix or identifier to the log file name, or there is any solution to handle it automatically?

### Operating System

Linux

### Operating System Details

Ubuntu

### FastAPI Version

0.128

### Pydantic Version

2.12

### Python Version

3.11

### Additional Context

You can use my example of code, or any other - stand your ground

Many thanks
questions.answer:
There are real problems with file logging when you run multiple Uvicorn workers (--workers N).

Each worker is a separate OS process. Stdlib handlers like FileHandler / RotatingFileHandler are thread-safe, but not multi-process safe. Multiple processes can interleave lines and break rotation (double-rotate, lost logs, rename clashes).

Uvicorn’s loggers (uvicorn.error, uvicorn.access) don’t fix this automatically. They’re just normal Python loggers configured by Uvicorn; if you point them at a file handler, you still have the same race unless you add a safe mechanism.

Best practice (especially in Docker/K8s): log to stdout/stderr and let the platform collect/rotate (Docker logging driver, journald, Loki/ELK, etc.).

If you must log to files on a single host:
- Use a multi-process-safe handler (file locking), e.g. concurrent-log-handler’s ConcurrentRotatingFileHandler
- Use QueueHandler/QueueListener (one writer process/thread).

As a simpler fallback: write one file per worker (PID in filename), then aggregate later.
Multiple containers/instances: don’t write all of them into the same shared file. Use stdout aggregation, or unique filenames per instance.

questions.title: Recommended Scaleable Web-sockets Libraries in 2026
questions.question:
### First Check - [X] I added a very descriptive title here. - [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it. - [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search. - [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information. - [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer. - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui). - [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc). ### Commit to Help - [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆 ### Example Code ```python from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket from fastapi.responses import HTMLResponse app = FastAPI() html = """ Chat

WebSocket Chat

""" @app.get("/") async def get(): return HTMLResponse(html) # TODO FIXME scale horizontally @app.websocket("/ws") async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket): await websocket.accept() while True: data = await websocket.receive_text() await websocket.send_text(f"Message text was: {data}") ``` ### Description * The docs link [encode/broadcaster](https://github.com/encode/broadcaster) which is now archived by owner and read-only. * Another recommendation from [Question 8684](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/discussions/8684), fastapi-socket.io is also now archived by owner and read-only. * Thus, I feel that the docs should be updated and am I looking for a recommendation with forward support. * What do people use and recommend? ### Operating System Linux ### Operating System Details _No response_ ### FastAPI Version Latest ### Pydantic Version 2.* ### Python Version 3.14 ### Additional Context _No response_
questions.answer:
Since `broadcaster` and `fastapi-socketio` are archived, here are the actively maintained options in 2026:

## Recommended Solutions

### 1. **python-socketio** (Most Popular)
```bash
pip install python-socketio
```

```python
import socketio
from fastapi import FastAPI

sio = socketio.AsyncServer(async_mode='asgi', cors_allowed_origins='*')
app = FastAPI()
socket_app = socketio.ASGIApp(sio, app)

@sio.event
async def connect(sid, environ):
    print(f"Client connected: {sid}")

@sio.event
async def message(sid, data):
    await sio.emit('response', {'data': data}, room=sid)
```

For horizontal scaling, use Redis adapter:
```python
import socketio

mgr = socketio.AsyncRedisManager('redis://localhost:6379')
sio = socketio.AsyncServer(client_manager=mgr, async_mode='asgi')
```

### 2. **Redis Pub/Sub Directly** (Simplest)
```python
import redis.asyncio as redis
from fastapi import WebSocket

redis_client = redis.from_url("redis://localhost:6379")

@app.websocket("/ws/{channel}")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket, channel: str):
    await websocket.accept()
    pubsub = redis_client.pubsub()
    await pubsub.subscribe(channel)

    async for message in pubsub.listen():
        if message["type"] == "message":
            await websocket.send_text(message["data"].decode())
```

### 3. **Centrifugo** (Production-Grade)
Standalone server, connects via HTTP API:
- Handles millions of connections
- Built-in Redis/NATS/Kafka support
- Dashboard included

GitHub: https://github.com/centrifugal/centrifugo

### Comparison

| Solution | Complexity | Scalability | Maintenance |
|----------|------------|-------------|-------------|
| python-socketio + Redis | Medium | High | Active |
| Redis Pub/Sub | Low | High | N/A (Redis) |
| Centrifugo | High (setup) | Very High | Active |

**My recommendation**: Start with `python-socketio` + Redis adapter. It's the most documented and actively maintained option for FastAPI in 2026.

### Description

FastAPI currently supports translations in 13 languages (de, en, es, fr, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, uk, zh, zh-hant), but Arabic (العربية) is not yet available.

Arabic is spoken by over 400 million people and is widely used in the growing tech communities across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA region). Many Arabic-speaking developers use FastAPI in production, and having documentation in Arabic would significantly lower the barrier to entry.

### What I'd like to contribute

I'd like to start an Arabic translation following the [Contributing to translations](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/contributing/#translations) guide. I would begin with:

1. `docs/ar/docs/index.md` (landing page)
2. `docs/ar/docs/tutorial/first-steps.md` (getting started)
3. `docs/ar/docs/tutorial/path-params.md` (path parameters)

### Notes

- Arabic is an RTL (right-to-left) language, which may require some CSS/layout considerations in the MkDocs theme
- I'm a native Arabic speaker and active FastAPI user (using it in a healthcare RAG application)
- Happy to coordinate with other Arabic-speaking contributors

Would love to get approval before starting work on this. Thanks! 🚀

Hello, thanks for your question.

## TL;DR

No, it is currently not possible to specify the log level (e.g., `--log-level debug`) using the `fastapi run` or `fastapi dev` commands.

## Explanation

The `fastapi` CLI presently hardcodes the logging configuration for the underlying Uvicorn server to `INFO` (ref code [1](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi-cli/blob/main/src/fastapi_cli/utils/cli.py#L23-L62) and [2](https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi-cli/blob/main/src/fastapi_cli/cli.py#L232)). It does not expose a flag to change this, nor does it respect standard environment variables like `UVICORN_LOG_LEVEL` because the explicit internal configuration overrides them.

### `--verbose` flag

You might have noticed a `--verbose` flag in the CLI help. For example: `fastapi --verbose run app/main.py`.

This does not enable debug logs for your application. It only enables debug logging for the fastapi CLI tool processes (like file discovery, import logic, etc.). It has no effect on the running server or your application logs.

## Workaround

The workaround available right now is to use `uvicorn` directly instead of the `fastapi` CLI as you have suggested or you can contribute to the fast API CLI source code by making this change, contributions are always welcome :)

### Example Code

```python
"""
Demonstrates the issue with BeforeValidator in FastAPI query parameters.

When using Annotated[..., BeforeValidator(function)] as a custom type conversion
in query parameters, the BeforeValidator function is NOT called.

However, the same pattern works correctly in Pydantic models.
"""

from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel, BeforeValidator

app = FastAPI()


def parse_comma_separated(value: str | None) -> list[str] | None:
    """Convert comma-separated string to list."""
    print(f"BeforeValidator called with: {value!r}")  # Debug: see if this gets called
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]
    return value


# Custom type using BeforeValidator
CommaSeparatedList = Annotated[
    list[str] | None,
    BeforeValidator(parse_comma_separated),
    Query(description="Comma-separated list of items"),
]


# This works - BeforeValidator IS called in Pydantic models
class RequestBody(BaseModel):
    items: CommaSeparatedList


@app.post("/body")
def with_body(body: RequestBody):
    """POST endpoint with body - BeforeValidator WORKS here."""
    return {"items": body.items}


@app.get("/items-none")
def items_none(items: CommaSeparatedList | None = None):
    """GET endpoint with query param - BeforeValidator does NOT work here.

    Expected: items="a,b,c" should be parsed to ["a", "b", "c"]
    Actual:
        v0.118.1: items = ["a", "b", "c"] (works)
        v0.118.2: items = None (before validator is not called)
        v0.128.0: items = None (before validator is not called)
    """
    return {"items": items}


@app.get("/items-no-validator")
def items_no_validator(items: CommaSeparatedList = None):
    """GET endpoint with query param - BeforeValidator does NOT work here.

    Expected: items="a,b,c" should be parsed to ["a", "b", "c"]
    Actual:
        v0.118.1: items = ["a,b,c"] (before validator called with ['a,b,c'])
        v0.118.2: items = ["a,b,c"] (before validator called with ['a,b,c'])
        v0.128.0: items = ["a,b,c"] (before validator called with ['a,b,c'])

    Note:
        if we remove the Query annotation with

        `
        CommaSeparatedList = Annotated[
            list[str] | None,
            BeforeValidator(parse_comma_separated),
        ]
        ```
        then it's None

    """
    return {"items": items}


def test_body():
    """POST with body - BeforeValidator WORKS here."""
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.post("/body", json={"items": "a,b,c"})
    print("POST /body with items='a,b,c'")
    print("  Expected: ['a', 'b', 'c'] (3 items)")
    print(f"  Response: {response.json()}")
    print()


def test_items_none():
    """GET with query param - BeforeValidator does NOT work here."""
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/items-none", params={"items": "a,b,c"})
    print("GET /items-none?items=a,b,c")
    print("  Expected: ['a', 'b', 'c'] (3 items)")
    print(f"  Response: {response.json()}")
    print()


def test_items_no_validator():
    """GET with query param - BeforeValidator does NOT work here with 0.118.1 and 0.118.2."""
    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/items-no-validator", params={"items": "a,b,c"})
    print("GET /items-no-validator?items=a,b,c")
    print("  Expected: ['a', 'b', 'c'] (3 items)")
    print(f"  Response: {response.json()}")
    print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("Testing BeforeValidator with FastAPI\n")
    test_body()
    test_items_none()
    test_items_no_validator()
```


### Description

# FastAPI BeforeValidator issue

We use Annotated + BeforeValidator to automatically convert query parameters like "items=a,b,c" into lists.

Starting in v0.118.2, the annotation doesn't work as expected anymore.

## Description

When using Annotated[..., BeforeValidator(function)] as a custom type conversion in query parameters, the function is not called.


## Versions

- 0.118.1 works ok
- 0.118.2 has the issue.

Probably introduced in https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/12942

## Relevant links

Related: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/13440
Docs: https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/query-params-str-validations/#custom-validation

macOS

_No response_

0.128.0

2.11.9

 3.13.11

annotated-types==0.7.0
anyio==4.12.1
certifi==2026.1.4
click==8.3.1
fastapi==0.128.0
h11==0.16.0
httpcore==1.0.9
httpx==0.27.2
idna==3.11
pydantic==2.11.9

questions.answer:
Before 0.118.2 there was a bug and FastAPI failed to correctly recognize the list type if it was specified using `Annotated` inside the `Union` (like `Annotated[list[str], Query()] | None`).

In 0.118.2 that bug was fixed and FastAPI now parses this parameter as list and passes list with one element to validator. You can see this in printed log: `BeforeValidator called with: ['a,b,c']`.

So, to fix your code example you need to modify `parse_comma_separated` to handle `value` parameter passes as list:

```
def parse_comma_separated(value: str | list | None) -> list[str] | None:
    """Convert comma-separated string to list."""
    print(f"BeforeValidator called with: {value!r}")  # Debug: see if this gets called
    if isinstance(value, list) and len(value) == 1:
        value = value[0]
    if isinstance(value, str):
        return [item.strip() for item in value.split(",") if item.strip()]
    return value
```

And, you don't need to use union in `items: CommaSeparatedList | None = None` - just `items: CommaSeparatedList = None` is correct since `CommaSeparatedList` is already `list[str] | None`

questions.title: Bug: WebSocket validation exception crashes server due to invalid close reason type
questions.question:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket
from fastapi.exceptions import WebSocketRequestValidationError

app = FastAPI()


@app.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    # Trigger a WebSocket validation error
    raise WebSocketRequestValidationError(
        [{"loc": ["query", "token"], "msg": "Field required", "type": "missing"}]
    )
```


### Description

When a WebSocket endpoint raises **`WebSocketRequestValidationError`**, FastAPI’s default exception handler attempts to close the connection using **`reason=jsonable_encoder(exc.errors())`**. Since this value is a list/dict and not a string, the underlying WebSocket implementation crashes when it tries to encode the close reason.

Expected behavior:
The server should close the WebSocket cleanly with status code 1008 (Policy Violation) and without crashing.

Actual behavior:
The server raises **`AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'encode'`**, causing an abnormal WebSocket close (1006) and logging a server-side traceback.

This happens with the default FastAPI WebSocket validation exception handling and can be reproduced with a minimal WebSocket endpoint that raises **`WebSocketRequestValidationError`**.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Create a file `main.py` with the following content:

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket
from fastapi.exceptions import WebSocketRequestValidationError

app = FastAPI()

@app.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    raise WebSocketRequestValidationError(
        [{"loc": ["query", "token"], "msg": "Field required", "type": "missing"}]
    )
```

2. Install dependencies:

```bash
pip install fastapi uvicorn
```

3. Run the application:

```bash
uvicorn main:app
```

4. Open a browser and navigate to `http://127.0.0.1:8000/`.

5. Open the browser DevTools console and run:

```javascript
const ws = new WebSocket("ws://127.0.0.1:8000/ws");
ws.onopen = () => console.log("opened");
ws.onclose = (e) => console.log("closed:", e.code, e.reason);
ws.onerror = (e) => console.log("error:", e);
```

### Observed Behavior

- Server logs show:
  ```
  AttributeError: 'list' object has no attribute 'encode'
  ```
- Browser console shows:
  ```
  closed: 1006
  ```

### Expected Behavior

- Server should not crash
- WebSocket should close cleanly with:
  ```
  closed: 1008
  ```


### Operating System

Windows, macOS

### Operating System Details

macOS Monterey v12.7.6
Same on windows as well, Windows 11

### FastAPI Version

0.128.0

### Pydantic Version

2.12.5

### Python Version

Python 3.11.5

### Additional Context

![FastApiIsssue](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7548af6d-58c6-45a3-887a-d9c507287426)
![browser](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dd9b86aa-087f-4270-96ed-c3ddd2cb4032)
questions.answer:
I think `WebSocketRequestValidationError` is intended to be used during the connection stage only (before `await websocket.accept()`).

To indicate an error in input data sent through the opened websocket connection you can raise `WebSocketException`:

```
from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket, WebSocketException

app = FastAPI()


@app.websocket("/ws")
async def websocket_endpoint(websocket: WebSocket):
    await websocket.accept()
    # Trigger a WebSocket error
    raise WebSocketException(
        code=1008,
        reason="Custom WebSocket validation error occurred.",
    )
```

    time.sleep(3)
    return "test func function finish!"

@app.get("/test/{p}",tags=["sysm"])
def tests(): 
    print("test receive web request! ")
    r = test()
    return "ok!"+r

@app.get("/test2/",tags=["sysm"])
def tests2(): 
    print("test2 receive web request! ")
    r = test()
    return "ok"+r
```


### Description

use axios to sent 2 request
```
["a","b"].map(item =>{axios.get(`/test/${item}`).then(v=>console.log(v.data))})
["a","b"].map(item =>{axios.get(`/test2/`).then(v=>console.log(v.data))})
```

server log is 
```
test receive web request!
test receive web request!
test func start  9936
test func start  16512
INFO:     127.0.0.1:60413 - "GET /test/a HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
INFO:     127.0.0.1:60412 - "GET /test/b HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
test2 receive web request!
test func start  9936
INFO:     127.0.0.1:60434 - "GET /test2/ HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
test2 receive web request!
test func start  9936
INFO:     127.0.0.1:60436 - "GET /test2/ HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
```
it's means : 
     when app.get have path arg , requests is parallel processing。
     when app.get no path arg, requests are being responded to one by one。

In reality, the test function is a database update feature and cannot be cached. This means that every time the test is executed, the results are different, even though the parameters have not changed.

My design is:  
When the first request for test2 is received, add test to background tasks to run, and immediately return 'The task has started running.'  
When test is already running and a test2 request is received, return 'The task is already running.'  

But the current situation: when multiple test2 requests are received, they end up running one after another in a queue.  

I have looked for official documentation but could not find relevant technical details. I am seeking help here.

### Operating System

Windows

### Operating System Details

windows 10 


### FastAPI Version

0.128.0

### Pydantic Version

2.12.4

### Python Version

Python 3.13.1

### Additional Context

_No response_
questions.answer:
serve is correct, it's a browser issue. 
I sent the request using the console in the Chromium Edge developer tools.
I went to Stack Overflow, and luckily, I guessed a few keywords for the search and found a related question from three years ago.
Among the many answers, I found a clue. The reason for this phenomenon is a browser issue. Any browser with the Chromium core may have this problem.

Conclusion:
Chromium will intercept the same GET requests and try to wait for the results to establish a cache. When connecting to 127 local, it may allow multiple requests to execute one by one because of the local client-server setup. When calling remotely, only one request remains.
At the same time, I rewrote the consecutive requests using Python and Node.js and got the expected results.

Stack Overflow really lives up to its reputation!

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated, Literal

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query, Depends
from pydantic import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()

class ItemParams(BaseModel):
    item_id: int | None = None
  
    @field_validator("item_id", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def return_none_if_undefined(cls, v: str):
        if v in ["undefined", "null", ""]:
            return None

        return v

@app.get("/items")
async def get_items(
    ItemParams: Depends()
) -> None:
    pass

if __name__ == "__main__":
    from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

    client = TestClient(app)
    response = client.get("/items?item_id=''")
    assert response.status_code == 200  # Expected 200 not 422
```


### Description

As the title says, `@field_validator("item_id", mode="before")` doesn’t seem to work for FastAPI query parameters. I spent hours debugging and thought it was a Pydantic bug at first, but the same validator works perfectly when used in the request body.

You can reproduce the issue by copy-pasting the code above—it returns a 422 error.

### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.124.0

### Pydantic Version

2.10.3

### Python Version

3.11

### Additional Context

_No response_
questions.answer:
Using Pydantic model to declare Query parameter this way (with `Depends()`) was never officially supported by FastAPI.

The correct way to declare Query parameters with Pydantic models is described in https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/query-param-models/

```py
from typing import Annotated

from fastapi import FastAPI, Query
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from pydantic import BaseModel, field_validator

app = FastAPI()


class ItemParams(BaseModel):
    item_id: int | None = None

    @field_validator("item_id", mode="before")
    @classmethod
    def return_none_if_undefined(cls, v: str):
        if v in ["undefined", "null", ""]:
            print("Converting to None")
            return None

        return v


@app.get("/items")
async def get_items(q: Annotated[ItemParams, Query()]) -> None:
    pass


client = TestClient(app)


def test_pass_empty_str():
    response = client.get("/items?item_id=")
    assert response.status_code == 200


def test_pass_undefined_str():
    response = client.get("/items?item_id=undefined")
    assert response.status_code == 200

```

Also, FastAPI treats empty string passed as Query parameter as not passing the parameter. So, default value is used and will be passed to validator

questions.question:
### First Check

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.
- [X] I used the GitHub search to find a similar question and didn't find it.
- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
- [X] I already searched in Google "How to X in FastAPI" and didn't find any information.
- [X] I already read and followed all the tutorial in the docs and didn't find an answer.
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Pydantic](https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [Swagger UI](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui).
- [X] I already checked if it is not related to FastAPI but to [ReDoc](https://github.com/Redocly/redoc).

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from typing import Annotated, Union
from pydantic import BaseModel, Tag, Discriminator
from fastapi import FastAPI, Body

class Cat(BaseModel):
    pet_type: str = "cat"
    meows: int

class Dog(BaseModel):
    pet_type: str = "dog"
    barks: float

def get_pet_type(v):
    if isinstance(v, dict):
        return v.get("pet_type", "")
    return getattr(v, "pet_type", "")

# Define discriminated union
Pet = Annotated[
    Union[
        Annotated[Cat, Tag("cat")],
        Annotated[Dog, Tag("dog")]
    ],
    Discriminator(get_pet_type)
]

app = FastAPI()

# ✅ THIS WORKS in 0.124.1+
@app.post("/pet/works")
async def create_pet_works(pet: Pet = Body(...)):
    return pet

# ❌ THIS BREAKS in 0.124.1+ (worked in 0.124.0)
@app.post("/pet/broken")
async def create_pet_broken(pet: Annotated[Pet, Body(...)]):
    return pet
```


### Description

I'm experiencing a breaking change when upgrading from FastAPI 0.124.0 to
   0.124.1/0.124.2.

   What works:

     - FastAPI 0.124.0 - Both endpoint patterns work correctly
     - FastAPI 0.124.1+ - Only pet: Pet = Body(...) works

   What breaks:

     - FastAPI 0.124.1+ - The pattern pet: Annotated[Pet, Body(...)] fails
   with:

     pydantic.errors.PydanticUserError: `Tag` not provided for choice {
       'type': 'tagged-union',
       'choices': {
         'cat': {'type': 'definition-ref', 'metadata':
   {'pydantic_internal_union_tag_key': 'cat'}},
         'dog': {'type': 'definition-ref', 'metadata':
   {'pydantic_internal_union_tag_key': 'dog'}}
       },
       'discriminator': <function get_pet_type at 0x...>
     } used with `Discriminator`

     For further information visit
   https://errors.pydantic.dev/2.12/u/callable-discriminator-no-tag

   Root Cause: This appears to be caused by commit 42b250d (https://github.com
   /fastapi/fastapi/commit/42b250d14dd42d3c0c24dd085fa53878172a985f) which
   fixed arbitrary_types_allowed=True but introduced a regression in how
   discriminated unions are handled.

   The change in fastapi/_compat/v2.py now includes *self.field_info.metadata
   when creating TypeAdapters, which causes discriminator metadata to be
   duplicated/nested when the union is wrapped in Annotated[..., Body(...)].

   Workaround: Use pet: Pet = Body(...) instead of pet: Annotated[Pet,
   Body(...)]


### Operating System

Linux, macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.124.2

### Pydantic Version

2.12.5

### Python Version

3.12

### Additional Context

 - The error shows tags ARE present ('pydantic_internal_union_tag_key':
   'cat'), so Pydantic sees them but validation fails
     - This only affects callable discriminators with Tag(), not field-based
   discriminators with Literal
     - Both patterns (= Body(...) and Annotated[..., Body(...)]) should be
   functionally equivalent
     - This is a breaking change in a patch release

   Is this a known issue? Should I file a bug report?
questions.answer:
Thanks for the report! I created an issue here: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/14508

I'm looking at this now.

I fixed it here: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/pull/14512, it is now available in FastAPI 0.124.3 :tada:

Hello

create_folder function is catching it, and then returns a JSONResponse with a comprehensive message in detail key.

>       self.assertEqual(

E       AssertionError: '53 validation errors:\n  A\n  s\n  s\n  i[241 chars]n  .' != 'Assigned user with email unknown@email.com not found.'
E       + Assigned user with email unknown@email.com not found.

E       -   s
E       -   i
E       -   g
E       -   n
E       -   e
E       -   d
```

questions.answer:
Actually, I think I found the issue.
`ValidationException` has one positional argument `errors: Sequence[Any]` and you are passing a single string to it. This string is also a sequence of strings (sequence of characters).
Try raising the error passing a list with that single string:

```diff
def create_or_update_folder(...):
    user = get_user_by_email(db, assigned_user_email)
    if not user:
        raise UserWithEmailNotFound(
-            f"Assigned user with email {assigned_user_email} not found."
+            [f"Assigned user with email {assigned_user_email} not found."]
        )
```

Or, modify `UserWithEmailNotFound` to accept `error: str` and pass it to parent constructor as `errors=[error]`

# TypeError: BaseModel.validate() takes 2 positional arguments but 3 were given
```

And, there is a closed issue in Pydantic repo: https://github.com/pydantic/pydantic/issues/9682

So, I'm not sure we can do something here..

---

As a workaround, try using Root model to define response model:

```py
from fastapi import FastAPI
from pydantic.v1 import BaseModel

app = FastAPI()


class Item(BaseModel):
    name: str

class Container(BaseModel):
    __root__: dict[str, str | Item]

@app.put("/items/{item_id}", response_model=Container)
async def update_item(item_id: str, item: Item):
    results = {"item_id": item_id, "item": item}
    return results
```

### Commit to Help

- [X] I commit to help with one of those options 👆

### Example Code

```python
from fastapi import FastAPI
from fastapi.openapi.utils import get_openapi
from pydantic import BaseModel, computed_field

class ModelWithComputedField(BaseModel):
    name: str

    @computed_field
    @property
    def computed_name(self) -> str:
        return f"computed_{self.name}"

class SimpleModel(BaseModel):
      value: str

app = FastAPI()

@app.get("/with-computed")
def route_with_computed() -> ModelWithComputedField:
    """Route returning a model with computed fields."""
    return ModelWithComputedField(name="test")

@app.get("/without-computed")
def route_without_computed() -> SimpleModel:
    """Route returning a simple model (no computed fields)."""
    return SimpleModel(value="test")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # This will raise KeyError when both routes are present
    schema = get_openapi(
        title="Test App",
        version="1.0.0",
        routes=app.routes,
        separate_input_output_schemas=False,  # Bug only occurs with False
    )
```


### Description

FastAPI 0.123.4 added support for computed fields in OpenAPI schemas (#13207) when `separate_input_output_schemas=False`, but the implementation has a bug where the schema generation crashes with a `KeyError` if the FastAPI app contains both:

1. Routes with response models that have computed fields
2. Routes with response models that don't have computed fields (e.g., dict responses or BaseModels without computed fields)

### Expected Behavior

  OpenAPI schema should generate successfully with computed fields included in models that have them, regardless of mixing route types.

### Current Behavior

  ```python
  File "../python3.13/site-packages/fastapi/_compat/v2.py", line 192, in get_schema_from_model_field
    json_schema = field_mapping[(field, override_mode or field.mode)]
                  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
KeyError: (ModelField(field_info=FieldInfo(annotation=SimpleModel, required=True), name='Response_route_without_computed_without_computed_get', mode='serialization'), 'validation')
```

### Operating System

macOS

### Operating System Details

_No response_

### FastAPI Version

0.123.4 

### Pydantic Version

2.12.4

### Python Version

3.13.8

### Additional Context

Workaround: Generate schemas separately for routes with and without computed fields, then merge them.

Looking at the PR that introduced this (#13207), the tests don't cover the scenario of mixing routes with and without computed fields, which is why this bug wasn't caught.

- [X] I added a very descriptive title here.

- [X] I searched the FastAPI documentation, with the integrated search.
